title: Kekkaishi
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Junior-high student Yoshimori Sumimura and his neighbour Tokine Yukimura are heirs of two feuding families of barrier-magic users who guard their school's land, Karasumori, from the ayakashi drawn to its power. Over 35 volumes they learn the founding legend is full of lies: the power comes from the sealed son of the clan founder, harmed by forbidden arts, and the story ends with Yoshimori's mother sacrificing herself to seal him and the feud laid to rest (Wikipedia).
life_message: Protecting others means facing the truth about your family's past and setting old wrongs right.

content.note: Ongoing battles with ayakashi, corrupt council members and a civil war in the Shadow Organization (Wikipedia; MU Exorcism, Demon/s).
Demons, ghosts and a power that drains life force (Wikipedia, MU).

dominant: Duty to protect; family legacy and hidden sins; growing up into responsibility

frames.aligns: Protecting the innocent; truth about family sin; self-giving sacrifice.
frames.concerns: Exorcism and spirit powers drawn from Japanese folk religion.

frames.aligns: Repentance for an ancestor's wrong; sacrifice.
frames.concerns: Spirits and demons as part of the world.

frames.aligns: Duty, courage and honesty about lies.

frames.concerns: Japanese spirit beliefs presented as real.

frames.aligns: Sins of the fathers and their consequences.
Clear moral frame; a lie exposed.

frames.concerns: Magic and spirits shown as real.

frames.aligns: Dharma of protector; karma of ancestor's forbidden arts.
Compassion for a sealed son; ending suffering.

frames.concerns: Ghosts and spirits shown as real.

frames.aligns: Sacred land, kami and purification of a polluted site.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Two families feud over who is the true heir of the art (Viz blurb, Wikipedia).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Hereditary duty to guard the land each night.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Clan inheritance and family feud drive the plot.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Council of twelve and family heirs hold rank.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Inherited techniques and legends, though the legend is exposed as a lie.

folkways.japan: Hereditary family roles, a crotchety grandfather and land-guarding duties reflect Japanese ie (household) and Shinto-folk norms, which the series depicts while questioning the founding legend.

delivery.evidence: Summaries show themes carried by plot revelations about the legend (Wikipedia); no review comments on delivery (to verify).
delivery.note: Lessons about inherited lies come through plot twists rather than speeches.

winners_losers: Yoshimori and Tokine succeed in resealing Chushinmaru; the corrupt Urakai founder is displaced and the organisation reformed; Yoshimori's mother gives her life. Honest duty wins over hidden ambition (Wikipedia).
to_verify: Violence and gore levels across 35 volumes (MangaDex safe; shounen battle series).
How the mother's sacrifice is framed (death or sealing).
Religious framing of kami, land-gods and exorcism.
